Status: planned, wave 2; repository not created yet, ad is the name proposed in the roadmap bibliography.
Forward and reverse automatic differentiation for Go (PLAN.md item 8, wave 2, size M). The organisation is to hold one library, proposed as ad.
No code exists yet: nothing on this page is released, measured or tested. It says what the library is planned to provide and how it will be checked. The wave and the order are in PLAN.md; the state of each item in STATUS.md.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be:
Reference tools are run as oracles, driven from Go by exec with JSON on a pipe; the unit suite must pass with no oracle installed.
Oracle How JAX uv run --with jax; Jacobians and Hessians as reference values Finite differences optimize.CheckGrad and ApproxFprime in go-numerics Analytic derivatives closed forms for the test functions What “correct” means:
Area Criterion Forward and reverse vs analytic exact to rounding; maximum relative error and ULPs reported Against finite differences agreement to O(h)

data.references#References:
The references the work starts from (bibliography first):
Griewank and Walther, Evaluating Derivatives, 2nd ed., SIAM 2008, doi:10.1137/1.9780898717761 Baydin, Pearlmutter, Radul and Siskind, Automatic differentiation in machine learning: a survey, JMLR 18(153), 2018 The Go language specification (no operator overloading; type parameters) Tapenade, source transformation
data.risks-and-open-questions#Risks and open: Go has no operator overloading (language specification), so AD is one of: dual-number types with explicit methods, a tape built by method calls, source transformation with go/parser, go/ast and go/types, or generics over an interface of operations. The design is not fixed. Retrofitting an existing func([]float64) float64 objective is only possible by rewriting a restricted subset of Go with go/ast. go-symbolic’s code generation is to emit gradient code that matches this tape (the reverse-mode sharing of Griewank and Walther).
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Forward mode dual and hyper-dual types with explicit methods (Add, Mul) Reverse mode a tape (Wengert list) built by calling tape methods, one sweep per gradient Jacobians and Hessians helpers, including forward-over-reverse Hessian-vector products Solver glue gradients for go-numerics/optimize and an AD-built Jacobian for integrate’s JacFunc
